subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this as a core multi-agent collaboration architecture, split it into narrower canonical tracks, or require plugin/API-first experiments before core adoption?
rationale: The answer changes core agent orchestration, session/memory state, config/defaults, provider dispatch, budget accounting, and security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product shape.

options.title: Split into staged tracks
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while #42475 owns spend budgets, #65403 or a successor owns meeting lifecycle, and separate design work settles blackboard, memory visibility, and SDK/API seams before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor a core architecture RFC
options.body: A maintainer explicitly accepts the broad core direction and authors or approves a staged design covering data model, security, config, provider dispatch, and UX.

options.title: Require plugin/API-first experiments
options.body: Keep core lean and ask contributors to prototype through plugins or external tools, adding only missing SDK and gateway seams when proven necessary.

recommendation.title: Split into staged tracks
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella while #42475 owns spend budgets, #65403 or a successor owns meeting lifecycle, and separate design work settles blackboard, memory visibility, and SDK/API seams before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest combination of related scoping discussion and current history across subagent, session-tool, and usage-cost boundaries.
